speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me pinpoint the cause, please tell me exactly how long these symptoms have been occurring and how many bowel movements you have per day.

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of relief with defecation, urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation suggests an inflammatory or infectious etiology; given your camping trip and sick contacts, did you notice any fever or blood in your stool recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein, Stool_Culture_and_Sentinel_Escherichia_coli.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inflammatory markers and stool culture are negative, which makes acute infectious colitis less likely; however, your normal white cell count does not rule out chronic inflammation. Did you experience any weight loss or a change in the size and frequency of your stools? REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin, Colonoscopy_with_biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative inflammatory markers and stool culture make acute infection unlikely, so we need to assess for chronic colitis or functional disorders; have you noticed any blood in your stool, and do you have a family history of inflammatory bowel disease? REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The repeat of normal inflammatory markers and stool findings makes active infection or classic inflammatory bowel disease less likely; have you noticed any abdominal pain triggered specifically by eating, and do you have a family history of irritable bowel syndrome? REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Elastase, Celiac_Serology_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see the Celiac serology and fecal elastase results are normal, which effectively rules out celiac disease and pancreatic insufficiency; to differentiate between Irritable Bowel Syndrome with constipation-predominant features or other functional disorders, do you have a history of anxiety or stress that correlates with your symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal abdominal ultrasound and previous negative workup for infection, celiac disease, and inflammation make organic pathology unlikely; do you have a history of significant stress or anxiety, and do you feel your symptoms improve when you are away from your usual environment? DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
